classifications.label: Instruments measure a common underlying oscillatory signal with frequency-dependent lag structure, but my readout or binning protocol introduces systematic phase drift that decorrelates readings from their own 5–8 day history while preserving cross-instrument structure at offset lags.

Each instrument is subject to independent random environmental noise (temperature, vibration, electromagnetic interference) that dominates the signal, but the noise has a characteristic timescale (~5–6 days) that happens to show up as anticorrelation when I lag-correlate, and weak cross-correlations arise by chance at the lags I chose to compute.

The settlement's experimental environment (magnetic field, acoustic environment, shared power conditioning, structural vibration) couples to all four instruments via a common mode, but the coupling is weak and my instruments have poor signal-to-noise ratio, so only the longest-baseline comparisons (pendulum_obs ↔ resonator_obs, both 60 trials) resolve it.

One or more of my instruments has a hardware fault (stuck relay, intermittent connection, capacitor drift, or calibration offset that shifts on a ~5-day thermal cycle) that I have not yet noticed because baseline-averaging hides the fault beneath the mean.
